Neither voice may be cloned from or resemble a real employee. Provider and voice ids pending program D10.

segments.narration: OMAR: In this module, follow a patient through a visit and see how Operations and My Care contribute at different points. Notice how their work connects.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: A patient who has to repeat their story can lose confidence in the visit. The teams need to connect their work so the patient is guided smoothly from one stage to another. As you look at the journey, consider what a clear handoff feels like from the patient’s perspective.
segments.on_screen_text: "Right team, first time." · A patient shouldn't have to tell their story twice.
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Follow the patient from booking through follow-up. Open each stage and notice when Operations, My Care, or both are involved. The sequence helps you see how separate teams contribute to one visit.
segments.on_screen_text: Horizontal journey: Book → Arrive & register → Consult → Lab / Radiology / Pharmacy → Leave → Follow-up. Each stage shows which team leads (Operations, My Care or both)
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Operations supports the day-to-day environment, monitors KPIs, and helps recover service when something goes wrong. As you explore these activities, consider what each one means for the patient’s experience and for colleagues working across the clinic. Some issues may need attention from another team, so be clear about the part you own and when a handoff is needed.
segments.on_screen_text: 7 items from slide 2, each with one example ("Recovery: a patient waited 40 minutes; the PX officer apologises and fixes the next visit")
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Use the chart to see how Operations is organised by role. Names can change, so the directory is the place to check current contacts. When a task needs support, identify the role involved and use the current directory rather than relying on a name you remember.
segments.on_screen_text: Redrawn role-only chart (B1): Director of Operations → PX & Operations Sr. Manager · Patient Access & PX Sr. Manager · Operations Sr. Manager → PX Managers → PXOs/FMs at sites J1–J4, PR1, VIP team, Check-Up Unit, In-Patient
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: My Care continues the relationship beyond the visit through follow-ups, programmes, and referrals. As you open each section, consider how those activities connect with what happened during the appointment. A useful handoff gives the next colleague enough context to continue the patient’s care without asking them to start their story again. That continuity matters to the patient.
segments.on_screen_text: 7 items from slide 5, with DMP/CHP expanded (B3)
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Explore the structure and notice how the roles fit together. The diagram can help you understand where responsibilities sit, while the current directory helps you find the right contact when people or assignments change. Use both when you need to orient yourself.
segments.on_screen_text: Redrawn role-only chart (B2): Director of Operations → Patient Access & PX Sr. Manager → My Care Manager → Onboarding leaders, site leaders (J1; J2–J4) → Coordinators; QA leader
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: Open each abbreviation and say what it means in your own words. Connecting the short form to its meaning can make team conversations easier to follow.
segments.on_screen_text: PXO · FM · Coord · DMP · CHP · HHC · PR1 · VIP team (B3)
segments.speaker: noor

segments.narration: OMAR: A request arrives during a busy shift. Read the details and decide how you would sort the work.
segments.on_screen_text: 10 cards → Operations / My Care: lab TAT KPI · clinic look and feel · on-spot complaint at reception · end-to-end journey · support a doctor's inquiry · monthly follow-up call · insurance medication follow-up · hypertension programme booking …
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: A patient needs help, and you are deciding where the request should go. Consider the situation and the support the patient needs before choosing a route.
segments.on_screen_text: 4 nodes (routing per B7): (1) A patient at reception is upset that her lab result isn't ready → Operations / PX officer on site; (2) A diabetic patient asks who will remind him about his 3-month review → My …
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: A concern needs escalation. Read the situation and decide what you would do next.
segments.on_screen_text: "The PX officer can't resolve a complaint on the spot. Who is the next step?" → site Patient Experience Manager (per B1)
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: You are working with colleagues across both teams. Match each role with its area of responsibility.
segments.on_screen_text: PXO ↔ "patient experience on site" · My Care Coordinator ↔ "follow-ups and bookings" · My Care Onboarding Leader ↔ "enrols patients in My Care" · Operations Sr. Manager ↔ "daily operations" · QA Leader ↔ "quality of My Care …
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: OMAR: Keep the patient’s journey in view: the right team, first time. When you need a current contact, check the staff directory. Then continue with the next module that fits your role.
segments.on_screen_text: Right team, first time · Link: live staff directory (intranet) · Next: module 05/06 (clinicians) or 08 (EHR)
segments.speaker: omar

segments.narration: NOOR: Carry that patient-focused approach into your next shift.
